summary: Both obligations are fixed. O-031: MainWindow no longer runs the volume-usage query on the scan thread. It never starts the query once Cancel was requested. Otherwise it runs the query on its own thread and waits on it only until Cancel, so a Cancel during a blocked GetDiskFreeSpaceEx ends the window's wait while the query finishes unobserved. The design doc records the decision and why this is used instead of a guard. O-032: the guard now reports LastCallAborted, which is true only when it refused the call or a cancel was issued during it, and DirectoryReader.List empties itself only then. A 995 that Windows returns with no cancel issued keeps its partial listing, is marked Unreadable(995), and the scan carries on. Two new tests cover this, at reader level and through the real scanner. The build has 0 warnings and the default suite passes 119/119.

files.why: O-031. The scan thread runs only Scanner.Scan. The volume query goes through the new UnlessCancelled, which skips it once Cancel was requested, and otherwise runs it on its own thread and awaits it with WaitAsync(token). A Cancel during the query ends the wait; the query finishes unobserved and the ending omits the volume line.

O-032. Adds LastCallAborted: set true when Enter refuses a call, and set by Exit to whether a cancel was issued during the call. Adds the test-only OverrideQueryError seam, which feeds an error Windows gives rarely (a 995 nobody asked for) through the real reader.
O-032. List empties the reader only when io.LastCallAborted is true. A 995 that Windows returns by itself keeps the entries read before it, as every other error does.

O-032. Adds A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelKeepsWhatWasListed at reader level and A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelIsAnUnreadableFolderAndTheScanCarriesOn through the real scanner. The existing abort test now also asserts LastCallAborted.

O-031: the Main window paragraph (line 46) now says a cancelled scan may omit the volume line, and the decision to await the query against Cancel rather than guard it is recorded with its reason. O-032: records that only the guard's own abort empties a listing.
O-031 evidence: the harness commands and output, and the report-mode run.
Harness that calls the built App's MainWindow.UnlessCancelled with a blocking query.
The published App in report mode on D:\. The scan finished and the volume line is still shown.

obligations.how: MainWindow now runs only Scanner.Scan on the LongRunning scan thread. The volume query goes through UnlessCancelled, which covers both cases the disposition names: it returns null without starting the query when Cancel was already requested, and otherwise runs VolumeInUse on its own thread and awaits it with WaitAsync(token), so a Cancel during the query ends the wait and the query finishes unobserved. I did not guard it in Core, because on a stalled share even CancelSynchronousIo waits for the SMB client (62 to 66 s in build 3). A harness calling the built App's own UnlessCancelled confirmed this. With Cancel before, the query never started. With Cancel during a query blocked for 30 s, the wait ended 2.3 ms after Cancel while the query was still running. With no Cancel, the result came back (42 after 205 ms). The query ran on its own thread. The published App in report mode on D:\ still shows the volume line when the scan finishes uncancelled. docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md records the decision, and its line 46 now says a cancelled scan omits the line. There is no App unit test, because the project has no App test project by recorded decision.

SynchronousIoCancel now sets LastCallAborted only when Enter refuses a call or Exit finds a cancel was issued, and DirectoryReader.List resets _count/_namesUsed only when it is true. A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelKeepsWhatWasListed injects a 995 at the third listing buffer with a live token that is never cancelled, through the new test-only OverrideQueryError seam: List returns 995, keeps the entries of the first two buffers, and the close runs inline. A995WindowsReturnsWithNoCancelIsAnUnreadableFolderAndTheScanCarriesOn feeds the same 995 through the real scanner: the scan is Completed, the folder is Unreadable(995) with its partial children, and the next folder is committed. Mutation checks: never resetting fails AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt, and resetting on any 995 (the old rule) fails both new tests.

deviations: O-031 is fixed by not waiting for the volume query, not by guarding it in Core. The disposition allows either. Build 3 measured that on a stalled, established session even CancelSynchronousIo waits for the SMB client (62 to 66 s), so a query guarded in Core would still hold the window. No architecture rule was added for the App, because its scan lambda now calls only Scanner.Scan; the decision is recorded in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md instead.
O-032 adds a third test-only seam to the guard, OverrideQueryError. Nothing else can make Windows return a 995 without a cancel through the real reader, which is what the new tests need.
follow_ups: A scan that completed without a Cancel still waits for the volume query. On a mapped drive whose server stopped answering, that can be as long as the SMB client waits. Cancel stays enabled during that wait and ends it. Whether to also skip the query for DriveType.Network roots is a product choice; the reviewer offered it as optional.

The stalled-session limit from build 3 still stands: a Cancel on a share that stops answering mid-listing waits 62 to 66 s for the SMB client. Only abandoning the scan thread, the design's rejected fallback, would shorten it. That is a decision for design-slice or a person.

Scratch folders %TEMP%\taad-sl024-o031, %TEMP%\taad-sl024-smb and %TEMP%\taad-sl024-respike, and the gitignored artifacts/publish, are left in place. Their evidence is copied into the slice, so they can be deleted.
